A fairly dry regime will continue for another day or so as moderate 
to fresh trade winds dominate the weather pattern. Shower and 
thunderstorm chances begin to increase for Guam and Rota late Sunday 
night as a broad trade-wind trough, with embedded Invest 95W, begin 
to lift west-northwest toward the area. 95W will gradually meander 
and wobble to the southwest of the Marianas through midweek as a 
broad disorganized disturbance, with convergence along its northern 
periphery inviting a slightly more unsettled pattern for the 
southernmost islands. There is uncertainty regarding timing and 
location of showers, as the movement of 95W will be affected by the 
path of TS Hagupit as it dissipates over the Philippine Sea, with 
models depicting some complex interactions between the remnants of 
Hagupit, 95W, and a broad frontal system farther north. For the time 
being, a generally more unsettled pattern is expected to bring 
periods of low-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms, 
mainly around Guam and Rota, from around Sunday night through at 
least Tuesday.

Marine...
Moderate to fresh trade winds will continue through the weekend,
sustained by the pressure gradient between the subtropical ridge
to the north and the unsettled pattern over western and central
Micronesia. Trade winds and swell will diminish early next week 
as the pressure gradient slackens, with light to moderate winds 
expected by Tuesday. Combined seas of 7 to 9 feet will relax by 
several feet through the first half of next week, becoming 3 to 5 
feet around Wednesday onward. Meanwhile, a high risk of rip currents
will continue along east facing reefs due to the elevated east- 
northeast trade swell, which is expected to persist through the 
weekend. The high risk of rip currents was extended, as the trade 
winds and swell will be slow to diminish over the next few days. 
There is also a moderate risk along north and south facing reefs. 
There will be a moderate risk for thunder Sunday night through 
Tuesday for Guam and Rota.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Hagupit is centered near 10N135E just northeast of 
Palau and west of Yap. The system is moving north-northwest at 
around 10 mph, with maximum sustained winds of 40 mph extending 
outward from the center up to around 110 miles to the northeast, with
lesser winds elsewhere. After a short burst of development along its
southwestern peripheries yesterday, the system continued to struggle
to develop any further overnight, with the bulk of the convection 
remaining near the center and skewed east and northeast; some 
thunderstorms are observed to periodically develop throughout the day
along the outer southwest peripheries near Palau, but are quick to 
dissipate as the system struggles to feed in more moisture and vent 
properly. Hagupit is expected to continue to move into the Philippine
Sea and begin to weaken overnight, likely to lose its TS 
characteristics Sunday and evaporate just east of the Philippines 
sometime in the first half of next week.

For more information on Tropical Storm Hagupit please refer to 
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header 
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header 
WTPQ31 PGUM.

A weak tropical disturbance, dubbed Invest 95W by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), is located around 7N153E, embedded 
within a broad trough extending north-northeast across Chuuk State. 
The northern edge of the trough, and 95W, are seen just east of 
Weno. Invest 95W is rated as a sub-low, meaning that development 
into a tropical cyclone is not expected over the next few days. 
Numerous heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms are seen along the
northeastern portion of the trough where it interacts with the trades,
just over Pohnpei and to the west, well displaced from the low-level
circulation center. 95W looks to lift west-northwest across Chuuk 
State and eastern Yap State over the next few days, promoting
increased showers and thunderstorms across central Micronesia, with 
little development expected.

Eastern Micronesia...
A moderately active trade-wind pattern is expected to be the primary
driver of weather across eastern Micronesia for much of the forecast
period. A building convergence zone ahead of a broad trade-wind
trough downstream will induce higher shower and thunderstorm 
coverage at Pohnpei beginning late tonight and lasting through 
possibly Sunday night, followed by another drying cycle that will 
bring back lower-end patchy showers and some thunderstorms 
thereafter. Meanhwile at Kosrae, a surge in the trades will continue
to bring more intense showers and thunderstorms tonight, before
tapering down considerably beginning Sunday as the moisture moves
toward Pohnpei to the west. This will allow the drier trade-wind
regime to last through the first half of next week, followed by a
return of on-and-off showers following another trade-wind surge. A
